# CommandMate — Run multiple coding agents in parallel — even away from your desk.

> CommandMate puts the coding agents you already use in one place on your own machine, so you can run them side by side, hand them work one issue at a time, and let your own checks decide when the work is done.

Open source (MIT) · runs on your machine · macOS / Linux / Windows (WSL2) · no app to install

Status: Beta. Set it up by asking your agent: "Read https://kewton.github.io/CommandMate/setup.md and help me set up CommandMate on this machine. Explain each step before you run it, and ask me before you install anything or open access from the internet." Needs Node.js v22+ · npm · git · tmux

One recorded run (PM → dev lead → workers):

- 4 issues, 4 workers (Command Code), PM and dev lead on Claude Code
- 2 messages and 3 taps from a phone-width web UI
- 4/4 checks passed, PRs merged with CI green, UAT 4/4 GO
- 9 min 48 s from request to report

As observed: one run, recorded on 2026-10-02. Not a benchmark.

Levels, by how much of the work a person still does:

- **Level 1 — Parallel** (your role: operator): Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, OpenCode (1.x and V2), Antigravity, Command Code or local models, each task in its own session, side by side. You answer each agent like a chat. It runs on the plan you already pay for and adds no pay-per-use API bill of its own.
- **Level 2 — Delegate** (your role: product or tech lead): one issue per Git worktree, a task handed over as a contract you can read later, and your own checks (lint, tests) deciding what is done, not the agent's summary. The method is installed as Skills.
- **Level 3 — Manage** (your role: owner): a PM agent plans the issues and hands each one to an agent, and only what passed the checks becomes a PR. You talk to the PM and approve; every step that changes something waits for your approval. The author's own cost for that team, the PM on Claude Max and the workers on Command Code Goat, is $110–$210 a month. Scheduled runs can start sessions at set times. The author's daily auto-fix run is the author's own setup built from scheduled runs and the orchestrate Skill, not a switch in the product.
- **Next — Learn**: not built yet, only a direction: use the record each piece of work leaves behind to improve how the next one is done.

Anywhere: at every level you can answer and approve from your phone, paired with `commandmate remote` through Tailscale or Cloudflare. Most people need only Level 2.

## Docs

- [Set up with your agent](https://kewton.github.io/CommandMate/setup.md): a guide for a coding agent to set CommandMate up on this machine, stage by stage, asking the person before it installs anything or opens access from the internet. Also printed by `commandmate docs --section setup`.
- [Documentation](https://github.com/Kewton/CommandMate/tree/main/docs/en): the English docs
- [Tutorial](https://github.com/Kewton/CommandMate/blob/main/docs/en/user-guide/tutorial.md): Use a sample repository with two bugs left in on purpose to work through the core of CommandMate in about fifteen minutes.
- [Setup guide](https://github.com/Kewton/CommandMate/blob/main/docs/en/user-guide/cli-setup-guide.md): install it for daily use
- [CLI operations guide](https://github.com/Kewton/CommandMate/blob/main/docs/en/user-guide/cli-operations-guide.md): every flag and every exit code
